critique.problem: The title states that the plot shows a causal relationship, when it cannot show causality.
critique.repair: Number of attended sessions for center and home based programs during Q1 and Q2

critique.problem: The y-axis starts at 76 instead of 0, which can exaggerate differences in the data.
The y-axis label does not tell us what Q1 or Q2 represents.
critique.repair: Include the unit of Q1 and Q2 in the y-axis label.

critique.problem: The two programs are differentiated by color, which could be unhelpful to someone that is colorblind.
critique.repair: Use differentiated textures to show differences in program.

critique.problem: The textures of each program are not different for each category, therefore are unhelpful.
critique.repair: Change the texture of one of the categories so that someone who cannot see color can differentiate.

question: Out of the visits recorded, how many of the weekly follow up exercises goals were met?
audience: This chart is meant for the rehab program coordinator in order to decide where to add follow up support.
intended_claim: Attendance percentage is very similar in both clinic and home-based programs, across both quarters
y_measure: The y axis shows the percentage (%) of weekly follow ups met.
grain: Each row represents one program per quarterly visit, with the number of patients seen that quarter and the percentage of patients that were successfully followed up with.
text_alternative: This is a line chart, with each quarter of visits on the x-axis and the percentage of follow ups met on the y-axis. There are two lines, one for the Home-based program and one for the Center-based program. This line chart shows that home-based follow up rate is lower than the center-based follow up rate, with the largest gap between the two being at the final quarter [70% for home-based vs 79% for center-based]. A limitation for this chart is that the patients were able to freely choose their program so the groups may be skewed due to possible confounders.
